findings.text: follow-on: the head arm's revision line names the base commit b29e1196e5ce2d96e21c2be61027d690477c9016 rather than the head a55ccd0f65415a1dcc95532310c5b702d30d6ccf the run landed at, so the log cannot by itself be tied to the commit under review; both base-gate.log:2 and head-gate.log:2 carry the identical revision line, and the only in-log evidence that the head arm ran the changed tree is the collected count (34 in head-gate.log against 30 in base-gate.log).

follow-on: the test table's row for test_audit_check_with_a_report_is_answered_from_it claims that test fails with its mechanism removed, but the recorded negative control ran 3 failed and 31 passed (negative-control.log), leaving this test green under the applied mutation; its red arm was never exercised, and the guard it does provide is the opposite direction (a report answering the row it also guards), which would only redden under a mutation the run did not apply.

justifications.fit: imas_codex/standard_names/review/jev_review.py:336 follows the module's derive-in-code idiom set by derive_dimension_decision at :111, and a search over imas_codex/standard_names/review for plan, sprint or ticket labels finds none in the changed module.
justifications.goal_fidelity: imas_codex/standard_names/review/jev_review.py:523 marks an audit check unanswered with no report and :527 derives its decision unknown, while :276 refuses an unsplittable Choice at table construction, so all three follow-ons hold.
